newsitem.title: SINGAPORE: Singapore HSFO seen steady amid Chinese demand.
newsitem.headline: Singapore HSFO seen steady amid Chinese demand.

text.p: High sulphur fuel oil prices on Wednesday were assessed steady from Tuesday amid more Mideast supplies seen arriving in the Far East and increased Chinese demand, traders said.
"There are at least four Kuwaiti cargoes arriving in the next two week," a trader said.
"On top of that we have our usual supplies from Iran," said the trader.
Some traders said Chinese demand will not be strong enough to absorb the surplus seen in the market. They said that part of the Chinese demand have already been met by South Korean supplies.
But strong bids were seen from a major oil company for two cargoes of fuel oil for loading in October at $116.75. Bids and offers on Tuesday were at $115-$117 per tonne.
October paper, was bid/asked at $115.50-$116.50, firmer from Tuesday's quotes at $115-$115.50.
